author: Midland Times
title: UT Austin honors energy icon Autry C. Stephens with naming of new engineering discovery building
text:
The University of Texas at Austin will honor the late Autry C. Stephens by naming its new Engineering Discovery Building after him. Stephens, a notable figure in West Texas energy development, was an alumnus of the university and founder of Endeavor Energy Resources. His company was sold to Diamondback Energy last year.
According to a news release, Stephens became one of the most influential independent producers in the region by recognizing and investing in the long-term potential of the Permian Basin. The new 210,000-square-foot facility is scheduled to open in 2026 and will house UT’s Hildebrand Department of Petroleum and Geosystems Engineering as well as its McKetta Department of Chemical Engineering. These programs are consistently ranked among the nation's best. University leaders state that the building reflects UT's role in fostering innovation within Texas' energy sector and preparing engineers for an industry shaped significantly by Stephens.
Stephens, who was born to peanut and melon farmers, earned both his bachelor's and master's degrees in petroleum engineering from UT. After serving with the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers and working in the industry, he founded Endeavor Energy Resources. He strategically acquired drilling rights across 350,000 acres in the Permian Basin, demonstrating patience through various economic cycles. The sale of Endeavor shortly before his death established it as the region's third-largest oil and gas producer.
University officials and the Stephens family express that naming the building after Stephens reflects his appreciation for his education at UT and his dedication to future generations. The Engineering Discovery Building will be connected to the Gary L. Thomas Energy Engineering Building and will include open research labs, flipped classrooms, new lecture halls, modern study spaces, and a redesigned Mulva Courtyard. University leaders emphasize that this facility aims to inspire future Texas Engineers to become innovators within the state's vital energy economy.
